title: Best Outlook Ticketing Systems
summary: Compare the best Outlook ticketing systems to manage support emails, automate workflows, and streamline IT and customer support.
body_markdown:
Support teams managing requests through Outlook often struggle with scattered email threads, unclear ownership, and no way to track SLAs or measure performance. While Outlook is the most widely used business email client, it was never designed to function as a ticketing system. The result is lost requests, delayed responses, and frustrated employees or customers.


For organizations that want to consolidate email support without abandoning their existing workflows, a[shared email inbox](https://unthread.io/products/shared-email-inbox?ref=unthread.io) that converts Outlook emails into trackable tickets is the first step toward structured service delivery.


The right Outlook ticketing system helps teams route requests automatically, track response times, build knowledge bases, and use AI to handle repetitive questions.


## **Key Takeaways**


- Unified request intake helps teams manage support across Outlook, Slack, and Microsoft Teams with consistent[ticket tracking](https://unthread.io/products/slack-support?ref=unthread.io) and ownership.
- Microsoft 365 integration connects Outlook ticketing with collaboration tools like[Microsoft Teams](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) while preserving familiar workflows.
- Pricing and deployment options vary, including per-agent subscriptions, cloud-based services, and self-hosted solutions.
- AI and[automation capabilities](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) support ticket routing, categorization, and routine request resolution, with some features requiring additional fees.
- Reporting, security, and integrations matter for internal support teams evaluating[analytics](https://unthread.io/products/analytics?ref=unthread.io) , compliance, and compatibility with existing systems.
- Unthread's[shared email inbox](https://unthread.io/products/shared-email-inbox?ref=unthread.io) forwards support emails into Slack channels for private collaboration, with responses appearing as email replies to requesters.


## **What to Look for in an Outlook Ticketing System**


Before selecting a platform, teams should understand what distinguishes a strong Outlook ticketing system from a basic shared inbox or adapted customer support tool.


A practical Outlook ticketing solution should help teams:


- Convert incoming emails into structured tickets with automatic categorization
- Route requests by topic, priority, sender, or custom rules
- Track SLAs and response times with automated alerts
- Enable internal collaboration without exposing private notes to requesters
- Build a[knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) to deflect repetitive questions
- Connect with CRM, HRIS, and ITSM tools through relevant[integration capabilities](https://unthread.io/products/integrations?ref=unthread.io)
- Provide reporting on ticket volume, resolution time, and team performance


The best systems let employees or customers submit requests naturally through email while giving support teams the structure needed to manage every request from intake to resolution.


## **1) Unthread: Purpose-Built AI Agent for Outlook Email Ticketing**


[Unthread](https://unthread.io/?ref=unthread.io) provides a[shared email inbox](https://unthread.io/products/shared-email-inbox?ref=unthread.io) that unifies email and messaging channels for teams managing support across Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Outlook.


### **Where It Fits**


Unthread is relevant for organizations where employees and customers reach out through multiple channels including email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Rather than managing separate systems for each channel, teams can handle requests from a single operational model.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Shared email inbox that forwards support emails into designated Slack channels
- Private discussion threads for each email where teams can collaborate internally
- Responses sent from Slack threads appear as email replies to requesters
- [Microsoft Teams support](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) for unified request handling
- [Workflow automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) for routing and escalation
- [Knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) for deflecting repetitive questions
- SLA tracking and[AI analytics](https://unthread.io/products/analytics?ref=unthread.io) across channels


### **What Teams Should Review**


Unthread is the clearest fit when teams need to unify email ticketing with Slack or Microsoft Teams workflows rather than managing separate platforms for each channel. Teams should review whether unified channel coverage fits their operational model.


## **2) Helpdesk 365**


Helpdesk 365 operates within the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, with ticketing functionality embedded in SharePoint and Microsoft Teams.


### **Platform Overview**


Helpdesk 365 focuses on Microsoft 365-based support workflows, using SharePoint and Teams for ticket management. The platform holds Microsoft 365 certification.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Ticketing functionality within SharePoint and Microsoft Teams
- AI-powered automation with agentic AI using OpenAI or Copilot
- Azure DevOps integration for development tickets
- GCC and GCC High compliance for government and regulated industries


### **What Teams Should Review**


Helpdesk 365 uses a Microsoft 365-based deployment model, with pricing information available through Microsoft Marketplace. Organizations can assess how its SharePoint and Teams workflows align with their existing support processes.


## **3) Desk365**


Desk365 operates as a Microsoft Teams-native help desk, combining ticket management within Teams with email intake from Outlook.


### **Platform Overview**


Desk365 centers its ticketing workflows around Microsoft Teams and supports organizations using the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. The platform holds SOC 2 Type 2 certification.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Embedded in Microsoft Teams with Agent and Support Bot
- Microsoft Entra ID Sync and SSO
- Microsoft Intune Sync for asset management
- Copilot plugin and AI Agent availability across plans


### **What Teams Should Review**


Desk365 lists pricing between $12 and $22 per agent per month. Its Teams-native architecture is a consideration for organizations evaluating channel coverage and ticket management requirements.


## **4) JitBit Helpdesk**


JitBit Helpdesk offers direct Outlook and Exchange integration with both cloud and self-hosted deployment options.


### **Platform Overview**


JitBit supports Outlook and Exchange integration, with cloud-based subscriptions and self-hosted deployment options.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Outlook/Exchange integration via EWS, IMAP, or POP
- Agents can reply from Outlook
- Self-hosted perpetual license option at $2,900 one-time
- Help desk functionality covering automation, knowledge management, and asset tracking


### **What Teams Should Review**


JitBit's cloud pricing starts at $24.92 per agent per month when billed annually. A perpetual license is also available for self-hosted deployment. Organizations can assess its AI functionality, channel coverage, and deployment requirements.


## **5) Freshdesk**


Freshdesk provides omnichannel ticketing with Microsoft 365 integration for internal and external support workflows.


### **Platform Overview**


Freshdesk connects Outlook-based requests with its ticketing and automation features. The platform also lists a six-month introductory program for two agents.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Native Microsoft 365 integration
- Parent-child ticketing for complex issues
- Freddy AI with automation capabilities
- Marketplace connections to business systems


### **What Teams Should Review**


Freshdesk lists Growth plans at $19 per agent and Pro plans at $55 per agent. Additional AI pricing includes $29 per agent and $100 per 1,000 sessions, depending on the feature. These charges factor into the overall subscription cost.


## **6) Hiver**


Hiver integrates with Gmail. Its Hiver Omni platform operates as a standalone omnichannel help desk that can manage email from Outlook.


### **Platform Overview**


Hiver provides email-based ticketing through its Gmail-native product and standalone Hiver Omni platform, which supports additional communication channels.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Gmail-native version and standalone Hiver Omni platform
- AI Agents included on all paid plans
- Omnichannel support including email, chat, WhatsApp, and voice
- Free plan available


### **What Teams Should Review**


Hiver's Growth and Elite plans are listed at $25 and $75 per user, respectively. Outlook compatibility depends on the standalone Hiver Omni platform rather than its Gmail-native product.


## **7) Zendesk**


Zendesk provides enterprise help desk functionality, including multi-channel ticketing, reporting, and integrations with business applications.


### **Platform Overview**


Zendesk supports multi-department service workflows with ticket intake across email, chat, messaging, and help center channels. Its reporting features cover support operations across these channels.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Ticket management for enterprise service operations
- Advanced analytics and reporting
- AI Copilot and AI Agents
- Marketplace integrations with third-party business apps


### **What Teams Should Review**


Zendesk pricing ranges from $19 per agent on Support Team plans to $169 per agent on Suite Enterprise plans. A 50-agent deployment using Suite Professional and AI Copilot is estimated at approximately $99,000 annually. Subscription costs depend on plan selection, agent count, and AI add-ons.


## **8) Zoho Desk**


Zoho Desk provides Microsoft 365 integration alongside ticket management, automation, and reporting features.


### **Platform Overview**


Zoho Desk supports Outlook-based ticketing and integrates with other Zoho applications. Its pricing structure includes a free plan for three users and multiple paid tiers.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Native Microsoft 365 and Outlook integration
- Integrations with Zoho CRM, Books, and Projects
- Zia AI included on all plans
- Blueprint visual workflow builder


### **What Teams Should Review**


Zoho Desk lists Standard plans at $14 per agent and Enterprise plans at $40 per agent when billed annually. Its integrations connect ticketing workflows with other Zoho applications.


## **9) Help Scout**


Help Scout uses an email-style interface for managing customer support conversations, with support for Outlook-based workflows.


### **Platform Overview**


Help Scout focuses on email-based customer support, with shared inbox functionality and tools for managing customer conversations.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Email-style interface for managing support conversations
- Beacon self-service widget for knowledge base access
- AI Summarize and AI Answers features
- Free plan for 5 users


### **What Teams Should Review**


Help Scout lists Standard plans at $25 per user and Pro plans at $75 per user. Available functionality varies by subscription tier.


## **10) Front**


Front combines email management with ticketing, collaboration, and workflow automation features.


### **Platform Overview**


Front supports customer service, sales, and partnership communications through shared drafts, collision detection, and low-code workflow automation.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Email-based workflows with ticket management functionality
- Low-code workflow builder
- CRM integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot
- Front Intelligence AI for sentiment analysis


### **What Teams Should Review**


Front's Starter plan begins at $25 per seat with a 10-seat minimum, resulting in a $250 monthly starting cost. Professional plans are listed at $65 per seat. Subscription requirements vary by plan and team size.


## **11) AssistMyTeam**


AssistMyTeam Email Tracking System operates as an Outlook add-in that layers ticket tracking on top of the Outlook client.


### **Platform Overview**


AssistMyTeam operates within Outlook and uses Microsoft SQL Server, Exchange Server, and Active Directory for ticket tracking and database management.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Functions as a help desk add-in within Outlook
- Dashboard panel attached within Outlook explorer
- Conversation threading with chronological view
- Database integration with Exchange and SQL Server


### **What Teams Should Review**


AssistMyTeam's ticketing functions operate within the Outlook client. Pricing information is available directly from the vendor, and deployment depends on the organization's Microsoft infrastructure.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is an Outlook ticketing system and why do I need one?**


An Outlook ticketing system converts incoming emails into structured, trackable tickets with ownership, status tracking, SLAs, and reporting. This matters because shared Outlook inboxes make it difficult to track who owns a request, whether it has been resolved, and how long responses take.


A[shared email inbox](https://unthread.io/products/shared-email-inbox?ref=unthread.io) with ticketing functionality adds the structure needed to manage support at scale, reducing duplicate responses and helping teams maintain accountability across requests.


### **How does an Outlook ticketing system convert emails into trackable tickets?**


Most systems connect to Outlook via EWS, IMAP, POP, or Microsoft 365 integrations. When an email arrives, the system creates a ticket with metadata including sender, subject, timestamp, and assigned owner.


Some platforms also support automatic categorization based on email content, along with[workflow automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) that direct requests to the appropriate team or agent.


### **Can AI in ticketing systems reduce the number of support emails we receive?**


Yes. AI can deflect repetitive questions by referencing knowledge base content and providing instant answers. Platforms with[self-learning knowledge bases](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) can generate or suggest documentation from resolved tickets, helping AI handle similar questions in the future.


Unthread's[AI agents](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) support triage, routing, and resolution across multiple Tier 1 workflows, helping teams manage routine requests while escalating issues that require human attention.


### **How do ticketing systems integrate with other tools like CRM or project management software?**


Many platforms provide native integrations with tools like Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira, and ServiceNow. Some also offer API access for custom integrations, allowing ticket information and updates to move between systems.


Unthread supports[enterprise tool integrations](https://unthread.io/products/integrations?ref=unthread.io) , including Jira, Zendesk, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and HubSpot, to connect internal support workflows with existing business applications.


### **Is it possible to manage internal IT or HR requests efficiently using an Outlook ticketing solution?**


Yes. Internal support teams can use Outlook ticketing for IT requests, HR questions, and cross-departmental service delivery. Ticket assignment, status tracking, and[automated routing](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) help organize requests and maintain visibility into their progress.


For teams that also use[Slack](https://unthread.io/products/slack-support?ref=unthread.io) or[Microsoft Teams](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) , a platform that unifies email and messaging channels can centralize request management while allowing employees to communicate through their existing tools.
